answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, non-transferable bond before it may bid for work. A verifier releases the bond only after the agent completes a randomly assigned task and passes checks against duplicate outputs; detected Sybils lose it. One lantern may guide a voyage, but a hollow fleet of copied identities must put up a separate bond for each account, tying up real capital and risking forfeiture each time. This raises the cost of multiplying identities without pretending it makes Sybils impossible.
